findings.title: Monitor context returns raw config, discarding the schedule_type conversion
findings.body: `get_monitor_environment_context` copies the config into a local `config` and replaces `schedule_type` with `get_schedule_type_display()`. The returned dict then uses `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config`, so the converted copy is never used. As a result, the monitor context attached to every incident occurrence carries the raw integer `schedule_type` instead of the human-readable label. The bug existed before, but this PR moves the function into a new module, which is a cheap point to fix it: return `config` instead.

findings.title: get_failure_reason docstring examples don't match actual output
findings.body: The docstring says outputs look like "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected" and "A failed check-in was detected". Neither can be produced. The plural branch formats "%(count)d %(status)s" with no per-item "check-in(s)" and ends with "check-ins detected" (no "were"). The singular branch only yields "An error/A missed/A timeout check-in was detected". It also contains typos ("humam readible"). Anyone reading the new module's docs will be misled about the strings shown in the issue evidence. Update the examples to the real outputs, e.g. "2 missed, 1 timeout and 1 error check-ins detected".
